findings.title: `queued` default evaluated once at import time
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a dataclass field default evaluated when the module is imported, so every `AssignmentSource` created in the process gets the same timestamp (the process start time), not the creation time. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` instead.

findings.title: to_dict/from_dict round-trip breaks across Celery JSON serialization
findings.body: `to_dict()` returns a `datetime` for `queued`, which is passed as a Celery task kwarg (`assignment_source_dict` in sync_group_assignee_outbound). With a JSON serializer this either raises a serialization error or, if coerced, arrives in the worker as a string, so `from_dict` will construct an `AssignmentSource` whose `queued` is a `str` (no validation catches it since `cls(**input_dict)` accepts any type). Serialize `queued` to ISO format in `to_dict` and parse it back in `from_dict`.

findings.title: New `assignment_source` kwarg may break existing sync_assignee_outbound implementations
findings.body: The task now always passes `assignment_source=parsed_assignment_source` to `installation.sync_assignee_outbound`. Any integration implementation whose signature does not accept `**kwargs`/`assignment_source` (e.g. third-party or plugin-based installations, and `IssueBasicIntegration` subclasses) will raise TypeError at runtime, silently failing assignee syncs after retries. Verify all implementations accept the kwarg or pass it only when present.

findings.title: where_should_sync does not forward assignment source
findings.body: `where_should_sync` calls `should_sync(key)` without a `sync_source`, so inbound paths that use it (e.g. `sync_status_inbound`, `sync_group_assignee_inbound`'s org filtering) cannot suppress cycles for status syncs. The newly added `assignment_source` parameter on `sync_status_outbound` is therefore never populated anywhere, leaving the status-sync cycle unaddressed despite the API change.
